newsitem.title: USA: NYS says to sell 20 health facilities, retire debt.
newsitem.headline: NYS says to sell 20 health facilities, retire debt.

text.p: New York State will sell 20 Department of Mental Hygiene properties around the state and retire $285 million of debt tied to the projects, Gov. George Pataki announced on Tuesday.
The "mothballed" facilities, which cost taxpayers about $40 million annually in debt service and maintenance, will be returned to communities and local tax rolls, the governor said in a statement.
Any proceeds of the sale after the debt is retired will be earmarked for mental health purposes, according to the statement.
All of the properties and buildings which are being sold are vacant and none of the current residents or clients will be displaced because of the sale, the statement said.

The Empire State Development Corporation will advise all state agencies on privatization initiatives and will issue an invitation to bid for the 20 properties. Potential buyers can bid on any or all of the surplus properties.
The state Legislature initiated the process with passage of the Mental Health Reinvestment Act of 1993. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
